content.title: PSG knocks out Liverpool to reach UEFA Champions League semifinals: Highlights
content.text: Updated April 14, 2026, 5:33 p.m. ETOusmane Dembele struck twice to confirm Paris St Germain's place in the Champions League semi-finals with a 2-0 victory over Liverpool on Tuesday, sealing a 4-0 aggregate win in their quarterfinal tie at a rain-soaked Anfield.The reigning champions soaked up sustained pressure from Liverpool, who were roared on by a raucous home crowd, but preserved the advantage they established in the first leg in Paris last week to book their fifth semi-final berth in seven seasons.Dembele scored at Anfield for a second successive campaign when he latched onto a ball from Bradley Barcola in the 72nd minute and curled a shot into the bottom corner past Giorgi Mamardashvili from 20 yards out. He completed his double early in stoppage time, slotting home a cross from Barcola.PSG will face Bayern Munich or Real Madrid in the semifinals with the Germans leading 2-1 ahead of Wednesday's second leg.– ReutersHere's how the match unfolded: Liverpool vs. PSG highlights Dembele scores again!With PSG already up 3-0 on aggregate, Ousmane Dembele scored his second goal of the match in the 91st minute, officially the nail in the coffin for Liverpool and the clincher that will send PSG to the semifinals. Ousmane Dembele goal! PSG up 3-0 on aggregateThe 2025 Ballon d'Or winner has surely clinched PSG's spot in the semifinals, skipping a shot past goalkeeper Giorgi Mamardashvili for the first goal of the night – making it 3-0 on aggregate. Liverpool penalty call overturned 60th minute: PSG still up twoThe game has opened up in the second half with Liverpool chasing two goals, with constant pressure being applied by the English side at Anfield. Halftime at Anfield: PSG 2, Liverpool 0 on aggregateIt was a scoreless first half in Liverpool with both teams looking dangerous at times but the Merseysiders suffering the major blow of Hugo Ekitike's injury.Hugo Ekitike injury: Mo Salah comes onLiverpool star Hugo Ekitike was stretchered off with a non-contact injury in Tuesday's Champions League quarterfinal second leg against Paris Saint-Germain.With around 30 minutes gone at Anfield, Ekitike slipped awkwardly as he was trying to change direction and reach a pass. The France star went down in obvious discomfort and immediately grabbed his right ankle area, sparking fears of a serious injury.Mohamed Salah came on in Ekitike's place in the 32nd minute.– Seth Vertelney Underway in Liverpool!The two sides are scoreless through 10 minutes at Anfield, with PSG holding the 2-0 aggregate advantage from the first leg in Paris. Liverpool lineup vs. PSG PSG lineup todayLiverpool vs. PSG oddsLiverpool vs. PSG prediction, pickPSG's two-goal cushion and first-leg control make it the heavy favorite to advance, though Liverpool's record of stunning European comebacks at Anfield keeps this tie interesting.Prediction: Liverpool 1, PSG 1 Bradley Barcola returns to PSG squadBradley Barcola has been named in the squad for their Champions League quarterfinal second leg at Liverpool. The France international had been sidelined for a month after suffering a severe ankle ligament sprain during the Champions League last-16 second leg at Chelsea.Barcola missed PSG's last three matches across all competitions, as well as France's friendlies in the U.S. against Brazil and Colombia."We’ll have to see how the training goes but whenever a player returns, it’s very good news," PSG coach Luis Enrique told a press conference on Monday. "It’s important for us to get our players back."– Reuters Anfield hosts Liverpool vs PSG showdownAnfield has long been a stage for European drama. In the 2019 semi-final, Liverpool famously overturned a 3-0 first-leg defeat against Barcelona with a stunning 4-0 victory at home. The atmosphere, manager Arne Slot said, could again prove decisive."Just as important as our performance is the influence of the Anfield crowd," he said. "We have to be much better than last week. Their players have experienced Anfield and think they know what is coming..."I think our fans are up for making it even louder, and that's also needed. I trust them to be even louder than last season."– ReutersHow to watch Liverpool vs. PSGWhen: Tuesday, April 14Where: Anfield (Liverpool, England)Time: 3 p.m. ETChannel/streaming: Paramount+ (WATCH HERE), ViX (Watch on Prime Video)
